We have for the last couple of weeks started to compile the Re-start/Integration Plans for Netco.  So far, we have primarily focussed on the mid/back plans where the technology requirements have been the driving factors.  Several plans are in the final stages of completion including:-

+	Infrastructure		Jenny Rub
+	Development		Jay Webb
+	EnronOnline		Webb / Forster
+	HR			David Oxley
+	Cash Management	Tom Myers
+	Credit			Debbie Brackett

The rest will be completed shortly.

We now need to focus on the commercial plans which have a slightly different focus. John and I would like to receive the plans "Re-start/Integration"  plans by January 7th, 2002 in order to go through them individually with each of you or in groups.  The focus should be to ensure that we have as much of the business up and running in the shortest time possible.  I have a suggested outline which you do not have to use but I thought it might help.  Please decide within yourselves the areas you will cover together or individually.

Customer Side	
+	Customers		Phase  1 - First Week (eg top 10)
				Phase  2 - First Month (eg top 50)
				Phase  3 - First Quarter (eg top 100)
+	Action Plan		Phase  1 Customers
				Phase  2 Customers
				Phase  3 Customers
+	Contracts by customers (pre-prepared with credit terms etc)
+	Customer visit schedule

Product Side
+	List of Products	Phase 1 - First Week
				Phase 2 - First Month
				Phase 3 - First Quarter

Target Number of Transactions
+	Phase 1
+	Phase 2
+	Phase 3

IT transfer 

Louise

propositions.text: Netco is undergoing a Re-start/Integration process involving multiple departments.
Several mid/back plans including Infrastructure, Development, EnronOnline, HR, Cash Management, and Credit are in final stages.

Specific individuals are assigned responsible for various plans: Jenny Rub (Infrastructure), Jay Webb (Development), Webb/Forster (EnronOnline), David Oxley (HR), Tom Myers (Cash Management), Debbie Brackett (Credit).
Commercial plans are pending and need to be completed by January 7th, 2002.
The objective is to have as much of the business operational in the shortest possible time.
Customer prioritization is planned in phased approach: top 10 in first week, top 50 first month, top 100 first quarter.
Action plans and contracts with customers will be prepared in phases with credit terms.
There will be a customer visit schedule linked to priority phases.
Product rollout is planned in phased approach similar to customers.
Target number of transactions have been set in phases.
The plan includes a focus on IT transfer.
Re-start/Integration Plans for Netco have been compiled over the last couple of weeks.
The initial focus has been on mid/back office plans where technology requirements were the driving factors.
Several plans are in the final stages of completion.
The remaining plans will be completed shortly.
The next focus will be on the commercial plans which have a slightly different focus than the mid/back plans.
The plans will be reviewed individually or in groups after submission.
The focus of these plans should be to have as much of the business up and running in the shortest time possible.
A suggested outline for the commercial plans was provided but it is optional to use it.
The areas to be covered can be decided by the recipients either together or individually.
The suggested commercial plan outline includes a Customer Side section.
The Customer Side includes Customers categorized into Phase 1 (First Week, e.g., top 10), Phase 2 (First Month, e.g., top 50), and Phase 3 (First Quarter, e.g., top 100).
The Customer Side includes an Action Plan section divided into Phase 1 Customers, Phase 2 Customers, and Phase 3 Customers.
The Customer Side includes a Customer visit schedule.
The suggested commercial plan outline includes a Product Side section.
The Product Side lists products categorized into Phase 1 (First Week), Phase 2 (First Month), and Phase 3 (First Quarter).
Target Number of Transactions are divided into Phase 1, Phase 2, and Phase 3.
There is an element of IT transfer involved in the plans.

upstream_policies.text: All sensitive business and property-related information—including details of property specifications, business operations, corporate agreements, negotiations, tenant data, and commercial plans—must be protected and accessed only by authorized personnel to prevent unauthorized exposure and ensure confidentiality.

All sensitive corporate information, including but not limited to business strategies, financial details, negotiation terms, internal plans, and contact information, must be strictly protected and not disclosed without proper authorization to prevent exposure and potential harm to the organization.

All employees must ensure that sensitive and strategic business information, including content strategies, marketing plans, product development details, and corporate strategies, is kept confidential and not disclosed to unauthorized parties under any circumstances.

All sensitive business and customer information, including negotiation details, client identities, contact information, business relationships, and collaboration data, must be strictly protected and not disclosed without proper authorization to prevent exposure and maintain confidentiality.

All internal schedules, meeting details, travel plans, and related confidential information must be protected from unauthorized disclosure to prevent exposure of sensitive operational and personal data.

All sensitive information related to risk management, including risk exposures, operational risks, financial risks, and security assessments, must be strictly protected against unauthorized access and disclosure. Access to such information is limited to authorized personnel only, and sharing outside of approved channels is prohibited to prevent exposure of sensitive data.

All strategic business, financial, operational, legal, and diplomatic information must be classified as confidential and protected from unauthorized access or disclosure. Access to such sensitive information is restricted to authorized personnel with a legitimate business need. Sharing or communication of strategic information outside the organization or with unauthorized individuals is strictly prohibited to prevent exposure and maintain corporate confidentiality.
All technical information regarding challenges, data loss, risk management, limitations, event details, and integration requirements must be classified as sensitive and handled confidentially.

All unreleased and sensitive corporate information, including but not limited to strategic plans, product details, operational procedures, and private discussions, must be strictly confidential and not disclosed outside authorized personnel.

All employees must not disclose or share any sensitive employment, location, identification, or personnel information, including job titles, work locations, personal contact details, and internal role assignments, to unauthorized individuals or external parties to protect privacy and maintain corporate confidentiality.
